t2508.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Salama b. Kuhayl al-Ḥaḍramī, Abū Yaḥyā al-Kūfī, as trustworthy, of the fourth generation.
as: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
سلمه بن كهيل متقن للحديث ، وقيس بن مسلم متقن للحديث ما تبالي إذا أخذت عنهما حديثهما
Salamah ibn Kuhayl and Qays ibn Muslim were precise in hadith, and you need not worry about taking their hadith from them.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
كوفي تابعي ثقة ثبت في الحديث، وكان فيه تشيع قليل، وهو من ثقات الكوفيين، وحديثه أقل من مئتي حديث
A reliable Kufan Successor, precise in hadith. He leaned somewhat toward the Shīʿah and was among the reliable Kufans. He transmitted fewer than two hundred hadiths.
He was reliable and transmitted many hadiths.
Abū Zurʿah al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
Yaʿqūb ibn Shaybah, quoted by al-Mizzī
Reliable and precise, with Shīʿī leanings.
إن حدثتكم عن ثقات أصحابي فإنما أحدثكم عن نفر يسير من هذه الشيعة: الحكم بن عتيبة، وسلمة بن كهيل، وحبيب بن أبي ثابت، ومنصور
If I transmit to you from my reliable teachers, I will transmit only from a few of these Shīʿah: al-Ḥakam, Salamah, Ḥabīb, and Manṣūr.
طلحة بن مصرف, quoted by al-Mizzī
ما اجتمعنا في مكان إلا غلبنا هذا القصير على أمرنا
Whenever we gathered, this short man, meaning Salamah, prevailed over us.
حدثنا سلمة بن كهيل وكان ركنا من الأركان وشد قبضته
Salamah transmitted to us, and he was one of the mainstays. Sufyān clenched his fist as he said it.
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī, quoted by al-Mizzī
لم يكن بالكوفة اثبت من أربعة: منصور، وأبي حصين، وسلمة بن كهيل، وعمرو بن مرة
No one in Kufa was more precise than four men: Manṣūr, Abū Ḥaṣīn, Salamah ibn Kuhayl, and ʿAmr ibn Murrah.

t2733.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Shabāba ibn Sawwār al-Madāʾinī, originally from Khurāsān, said to have been named Marwān, a client of Banū Fazāra. He is trustworthy and a memorizer, accused of Irjāʾ, among the ninth generation; he died in 204, 205 or 206.
as: He is trustworthy, a memorizer, accused of Irjāʾ.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
I left him and did not write from him because of irjāʾ.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
زكريا بن يحيى الساجي, quoted by al-Mizzī
صدوق يدعو إلى الإرجاء، كان أحمد بن حنبل يحمل عليه.
Truthful, but he promoted irjāʾ. Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal criticized him.
كان أحمد بن حنبل لا يرضاه، وهو صدوق في الحديث.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal did not approve of him. He is truthful in hadith.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
He called Shabābah reliable in transmitting from Shuʿbah.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
وكان شبابة أجرأ عليها، وجميعا ثقتان.
Shabābah was more confident in transmitting Warqāʾ’s commentary, and both transmitters were reliable.
ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī, quoted by al-Mizzī
كان شيخا صدوقا إلا أنه كان يقول بالإرجاء ولا ننكر لرجل سمع من رجل ألفا، أو ألفين أن يجئ بحديث غريب.
He was a truthful shaykh, though he held irjāʾ. It is unsurprising for someone who heard one or two thousand reports from a teacher to bring an unfamiliar report.
Yaʿqūb ibn Shaybah, quoted by al-Mizzī
وهذا حديث لم نسمعه من أحد من أصحاب شعبة إلا من شبابة، ولم يبلغني أن أحدا من أصحاب شعبة رواه غير شبابة.
We heard this report from Shabābah alone among Shuʿbah’s students, and I know of no other student of Shuʿbah who transmitted it.
Al-ʿIjlī affirmed that he memorized hadith.
فشبابة بن سوار أيضا؟ قال: نعم. قيل: رجع عنه؟ قال: نعم. قال: الإيمان قول وعمل.
Abū Zurʿah affirmed that Shabābah also held irjāʾ and later abandoned it. He said faith consists of belief expressed in words and deeds.
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
صدوق يكتب حديثه ولا يحتج به.
Truthful. His hadith may be written down but is not used as proof.
وشبابة عندي إنما ذمه الناس للإرجاء الذي كان فيه، وأما في الحديث فإنه لا بأس به كما قال علي ابن المديني. والذي أنكر عليه الخطأ، ولعله حدث به حفظا.
In my judgment, people criticized Shabābah for his irjāʾ. As a transmitter he is acceptable, as ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī said. The objection was to an error, and he may have transmitted it from memory.
وهذه الأحاديث الثلاثة التي ذكرتها عن شبابة، عن شعبة هي التي أنكرت عليه.
These three hadiths I have mentioned from Shabābah through Shuʿbah are the ones for which he was criticized.
والذي أنكر عليه الخطأ، ولعله حدث به حفظا
The criticism concerned errors, possibly arising from transmission from memory.
وكان ثقة صالح الأمر في الحديث. وكان مرجيا.
He was reliable and sound in hadith. He held irjāʾ.

t7976.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Makhzūmī, the Medinan, as trustworthy, a jurist and devout, of the third generation, who died in 94; his name is disputed.
as: وكان ثقة، فقيها، عالما، سخيا، كثير الحديث.
He was reliable, a jurist, learned, generous and a prolific transmitter.
He is one of the leading authorities among Muslims.
عمر، وأبو بكر، وعكرمة، وعبد الله بنو عبد الرحمن بن الحارث بن هشام كلهم أجلة ثقات يضرب بهم. المثل
ʿUmar, Abū Bakr, ʿIkrimah and ʿAbd Allāh, the sons of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith, were all eminent, reliable and held up as examples.
الزبير بن بكار, quoted by al-Mizzī
وهو أحد فقهاء المدينة السبعة، وكان يسمى الراهب، وكان من سادات قريش
One of the seven jurists of Medina, he was called the monk and was one of the leading members of Quraysh.
وكان يقال له: راهب قريش، لكثرة صلاته.
He was called the monk of Quraysh because of his frequent prayers.
Ibn Ḥibbān listed him in The Reliable Transmitters.

أدركت من فقهاء أهل المدينة وعلمائهم ومن يرتضى وينتهى إلى قولهم، منهم: سعيد بن المسيب، وعروة بن الزبير، والقاسم بن محمد، وأبو بكر بن عبد الرحمن، وخارجة بن زيد، وعبيد الله بن عبد الله بن عتبة، وسليمان بن يسار
Abū al-Zinād includes him among the Medinan jurists and scholars whose opinions were accepted as authoritative.
وكان يقال له راهب قريش لكثرة صلاته ولفضله.
He was called the monk of Quraysh for his frequent prayers and virtue.
عبد الملك, quoted by Ibn Saʿd
إني لأهم بالشيء أفعله بأهل المدينة لسوء أثرهم عندنا فأذكر أبا بكر بن عبد الرحمن فأستحي منه فأدع ذلك الأمر.
When I consider doing something to the people of Medina because of their poor record with us, I remember Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, feel ashamed before him and leave the matter.

t8186.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Abū Ṭuʿma, a Shāmī who settled in Egypt and was a client of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, said to be named Hilāl, acceptable of the fourth generation; it is not established that Makḥūl called him a liar.
as: ولم يثبت أن مكحولا رماه بالكذب
It is not established that Makḥūl accused him of lying.

t8591.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records another Rumaytha who narrated from ʿĀʾisha about nabīdh; she is not known and belongs to the third generation.

t904.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Jubayr ibn Nufayr al-Ḥaḍramī al-Ḥimṣī as trustworthy and eminent, of the second generation, a mukhaḍram whose father had Companionship; he died in 80 AH or later.
as: Abū Zurʿah al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
ليس أحد من كبار التابعين، أحسن رواية عن الصحابة من ثلاثة: قيس بن أبي حازم، وأبي عثمان النهدي، وجبير بن نفير.
Among the senior Successors, no one transmitted from the Companions better than Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim, Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī and Jubayr ibn Nufayr.
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
من كبار تابعي أهل الشام من القدماء.
One of the senior and early Syrian Successors.
I rank Abū Idrīs higher, though Duḥaym also held Jubayr in high regard.
Ibn Ḥibbān, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
قال ابن حبان في «ثقات التابعين» : أدرك الجاهلية.
Ibn Ḥibbān included him among reliable Successors and says he lived in the pre-Islamic period.
وكان ثقة فيما روى من الحديث.
He was reliable in the hadiths he narrated.
